title: Internal-composition equations for normalized coefficient reduction
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, an arbitrary scheme $W$ in an independent universe, and a coefficient fiber calculus $S$ [def-coef-derived-system-calculus-data]. Let $R$ be its explicit normalized reduction data [def-pur-canonical-coefficient-reduction]. For its reduction functor, and for each finite scalar-extension functor, the evaluation-defined base-change map preserves internal composition. Explicitly, for the relevant closed structures $A,B$, functor $F$ and conjugated tensor comparison $\mu$, and all derived inputs $P,Q,V$, one has $F(\operatorname{comp}_A(P,Q,V));\beta(P,V)=\mu_{[Q,V],[P,Q]};(\beta(Q,V)\otimes\beta(P,Q));\operatorname{comp}_B(FP,FQ,FV)$. Here composition is transposed iterated evaluation with the specified normalized associator, and $\beta$ is transposed reduced evaluation [def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model, def-coef-derived-system-calculus-data]. This is solely two families of morphism equations: it asserts no existence of a calculus, fiber-Hom comparison, enriched adjunction, or global comparison.

proof.text: Use the normalized closed structures on the integral, sequence and finite sites. Their associators descend the ordinary reassociation of total tensor complexes. The transported tensor models have the same ordinary uncurrying formula, by construction. Identify their comparisons with the fixed normalized duality-model comparisons by uncurrying into the fixed Hom resolution and uniqueness on sheafified tensor generators. The representative normalization equations compute the conjugated tensor maps by the old strict pure-tensor maps.

source.place: Tags 07A4, 08JD (lemma-dual), 0A98 (lemma-internal-hom-composition), 0941; canonical integral calculus, presentation-normalization steps 1--3.

proof.text: Uncurry the two sides of each internal-composition equation. On three homogeneous sections, the normalized associators reassociate the same total tensor and both maps evaluate phi(psi(x)). The signed differentials agree. Generator uniqueness proves the chain equation; K-flat localization in the variables and naturality along resolution isomorphisms give the equation for all derived inputs. Perform this on the sequence site itself for reduction, and on each finite site for scalar extension. This does not assume an arbitrary adjoint comparison is monoidal.

theorem compositionLaws (S : CoefficientDerivedSystemFibers l E W) :
    let R := reduction l E W S.toCoefficientDerivedSystemReduction
    CompositionLaw R.integralClosed R.systemClosed R.reduction R.reductionTensor ∧
      ∀ n : ℕ, CompositionLaw R.integralClosed (R.finiteClosed n)
        (coefficientFiniteDerivedExtension l E W n) (R.finiteTensor n)
